title: Injectivity of finite surjective pullback on set-sheaf sections
statement: Let $f:X\prime\to X$ be finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism], and let $G$ be a sheaf of sets on the small étale site of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets]. With section pullback $f^*$ given by the adjunction unit [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units], the map $G(X)\to(f^{-1}G)(X\prime)$ is injective.

proof.text: For two sections with equal unit pullbacks, use the geometric-germ extensionality lemma: it suffices to show that their germs agree at every geometric point and pointed identity neighbourhood.

For a fixed geometric point y, use surjectivity to choose an underlying point x\prime over its image. Finite geometric-point lifting supplies t with t f = y, over the same algebraically closed field. Substitute this equality.

Apply the inverse-image stalk comparison c to germs of the two equal unit-pulled-back sections at the pointed pullback neighbourhood. Congruence gives equality of these images; the two germ equations identify the images with the original germs. Transitivity proves the desired germ equality.

proof_origin.place: Remark 09Z3, injectivity of the diagonal, reduced directly to germs using 03Q1 (3) and 03PU

theorem finiteSurjectiveSetDescent_injective
    {X X' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X' ⟶ X) [IsFinite f] [Surjective f]
    (G : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (Type (u + 1))) :
    Function.Injective (etaleSetDescentUnit f G (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X)))
